_doc: YEAR-SIM-1 for every system (Rowan, 2026-11-21): "proving that it can run a year unattended in code and proactively mitigate and remediate all of its intended failure modes ... I want it in the core product." Read by scripts/yearsim.py (the portable runner; the engine is shared with the platform's foundation/yearsim.py). Each fault is a way an unattended year goes wrong, with a yearly rate that says whether it was observed or assumed, a duration range in days, and a `drill`: a command that injects the fault into this system's real recovery code and exits 0 only when the system recovers by itself. No drill means declared, not exercised, and is never read as a pass. The simulator multiplies the capacity of the faults active each day; a year ends when capacity stays under fatal_floor for fatal_after_days. The standing goal core.year.unattended (seed/autonomy/goals.json) is horizon p10 >= target_days. Sensitivity (each rate doubled and halved) names which faults move the horizon most. A system adds its own faults here; the generic ones below ship with every system. A fault may name `rate_from`, a key of ops/trajectory.json `observed` (scripts/trajectory.py): where the system's own history holds enough events, the observed rate and its trend replace the assumed one (TRAJECTORY-1).

faults.what: the platform scheduler skips scheduled runs
faults.basis: assumed: schedulers on shared platforms skip runs most weeks

faults.what: the code host (git, API) is unavailable
faults.basis: assumed: a few full outages a year

faults.what: the day's free AI allowance is used up
faults.basis: assumed: a busy day reaches the daily allowance

faults.what: a loop's spend jumps several times over its normal rate
faults.basis: assumed: a runaway loop or scan a few times a year

faults.what: two changes collide in a generated or append-only file
faults.basis: assumed: most merges touch ledgers or generated data

faults.what: a change is merged but its deploy or verify step fails
faults.basis: assumed: a deploy or verify failure about monthly

faults.what: an item leaves the queue with no recorded disposition
